title: Current Account Deficit

anim.title: India's current account deficit (% of GDP)

segments.say: In twenty twenty-two to twenty-three, India's current account deficit was two per cent of GDP. The next year it fell to under one per cent. What moved it?
The current account records a country's trade in goods and services with the world, income on investments, and transfers such as money sent home.
India usually buys more goods from abroad than it sells. That merchandise trade deficit is the main reason the current account is in the red.

Invisibles push the other way: mainly services exports and money sent home by Indians abroad. India received about one hundred and thirty-five billion dollars in remittances in twenty twenty-four to twenty-five, the most of any country.

anim.title: Paying for a deficit
items: Financed by capital inflows: investment and loans

segments.say: A deficit has to be paid for, by foreign investment and loans coming in, or by drawing on foreign exchange reserves.
In twenty twenty-three to twenty-four, a smaller goods deficit and stronger invisibles together cut the gap.
For GS Three, read any current account deficit in three parts: the goods gap, the invisibles, and how the rest is financed.

sources: RBI press release, Developments in India's Balance of Payments during Q4:2023-24: current account deficit moderated to US$23.2 billion (0.7% of GDP) in 2023-24 from US$67.0 billion (2.0% of GDP) in 2022-23 on the back of a lower merchandise trade deficit; net invisibles receipts higher, primarily services and transfers
RBI press release, BoP Q2:2022-23: the current account deficit was underlain by a wider merchandise trade deficit and higher net outgo under investment income
PIB (PRID 2219971), Economic Survey: India remained the world's largest recipient of remittances, with inflows of US$135.4 billion in FY25
Wikipedia, 'Balance of payments' (read): current account deficits are financed by capital account inflows such as loans and investments; reserves

quiz.q: What is the main reason India usually runs a current account deficit?
quiz.why: RBI links the deficit mainly to the merchandise trade deficit.

quiz.q: Which of these is an 'invisible' that helps India's current account?
quiz.why: Services exports and remittances are invisibles; loans are in the capital account.
